title: Tenant isolation sampling protocol — dedicated GPU pools
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight on-call sampling and containment protocol to use when a dedicated GPU pool shows intermittent throughput or latency degradation that might be caused by a tenant behaving poorly (high GPU occupancy, long-running kernels, pathological batch patterns) or an autoscaler/configuration issue. The intent is to gather reproducible telemetry samples, make a short-term containment decision, and capture artifacts for a follow-up investigation. This is not a full postmortem template — it's the emergency sampling checklist and immediate mitigation rubric for SREs responding to dedicated capacity incidents.

Scope and when to use:
- Dedicated pools (reserved GPU capacity) that host multi-tenant workloads.
- Triggers: sustained 10%+ throughput loss across a pool for 5+ minutes, p95/p99 generation latency spikes, or repeated eviction cascades that correlate with tenant resource spikes.
- Not for control-plane-only incidents (use platform-engineering runbooks).

Quick summary (first 12 minutes):
0) Triage lead: whoever picks up the pager announces in #sre-dedicated with short blurb: pool id, region, observable symptom, impact surface.
1) Take snapshot T0 (0–3 min):
   - Capture Prometheus queries and raw timeseries for the last 30m and 6h (see queries below).
   - Run "nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o TD 1 5" on affected nodes (collect a 5s sample if under pressure, else 60s).
   - Dump dcgm-exporter metrics: dcgm_gpu_utilization, dcgm_sm_active, dcgm_power_usage, dcgm_memory_used per GPU.
   - Record which tenants/containers are scheduled on the node (kubectl get pods -o wide; include pod name, namespace, resource requests/limits, affinity labels).
2) Contain (3–8 min):
   - If a single tenant is disproportionally high (GPU util > 85% and kernel duration high): throttle via per-tenant rate-limiter or move tenant to a lower-priority pool if cluster supports it. Command examples: 
       * rate-limit: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/ratelimit/tenants/<tenant-id> -d '{"qps":10}'
       * eviction: kubectl cordon/evict pattern; use eviction score script: /ops/bin/evict-heavy-tenant.sh <pod>
   - If autoscaler misconfig suspected (rapid flapping, min_replicas too low), temporarily set pool.min_replicas = max(pool.min_replicas, current_rps / expected_rps_per_node) and hold scale-down for 10m. Use allocator admin API: POST /admin/pools/<pool>/set-min?value=<n>
3) Verify containment (8–12 min):
   - Check p95/p99 latencies and throughput 5 min after containment action.
   - If improvement: continue to monitor and prepare follow-up.
   - If no improvement or broader nodes affected: escalate to incident (assign SRE lead, infra lead, and oncall product owner).

Sampling protocol (how to capture high-value reproducible artifacts):
- What to snapshot (label each artifact with timestamp and a short tag):
  * prometheus-30m-<pool>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.prom (timeseries response from key queries)
  * node-nvidia-smi-<node>-<ts>.log (nvidia-smi dmon/system)
  * container-cgroup-stats-<pod>-<ts>.json (cgroup blkio/cpu/memory stats)
  * dcgm-exporter-dump-<node>-<ts>.prom
  * kernel-stackshot-<pid>-<ts>.txt (if long kernels suspected: capture pid and cuda stack)
- Minimum queries to run immediately (PromQL examples):
  * rate(dcgm_gpu_utilization[5m]) by (gpu)
  * max_over_time(dcgm_sm_active[30m]) by (gpu)
  * sum(rate(requests_total[5m])) by (pool)
  * histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
  * allocator_evictions_total{pool=~"<pool>"} - look for spikes
- Collect a short flamegraph (kernel-level) if possible using short-run NVProf/ Nsight-capture on a quarantined node (requires coordination with infra).

Containment heuristics (decision tree):
- If one pod/tenant accounts for >50% GPU utilization across node(s) -> isolate that pod (evict or throttle).
- If several tenants spike simultaneously -> check for autoscaler-induced oscillation (look for synchronized scale events across tenants in logs). If so, pause scale-down for 10–20m and fix hysteresis in autoscaler config.
- If device-level telemetry shows thermal throttling / ECC errors -> treat as hardware issue, notify infra and move tenants off node immediately.
- If memory pressure on GPU causes out-of-memory OOMs -> lower batch sizes for offending tenant via config override if supported.

Common commands and one-liners (examples for oncall use):
- List pods on node: kubectl get pods --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,NS:.metadata.namespace,REQ:.spec.containers[0].resources.requests
- Dump nvidia-smi: ssh node && sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-snapshot.csv
- DCGM exporter: curl http://<node>:9100/metrics | grep dcgm
- Evict a pod (graceful): kubectl delete pod <pod> -n <ns> --grace-period=30
- Pause allocator scale-down (admin API): curl -X POST https://allocator.internal/api/pools/<pool>/pause-scale-down -d '{"duration":"10m"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'

Notes about autoscaler misconfiguration signs:
- Frequent add/remove cycles in a short period (>=3 changes in 10 minutes) correlated with small RPS changes.
- Scale decisions made on a noisy metric (e.g., per-second request spikes) rather than a smoothed metric.
- Missing or too-short cooldown windows.
- Suggested quick fix: increase cooldown, add a 1–2 minute smoothing window, and introduce a minimum replica floor for the pool.

Post-incident capture checklist (if incident declared):
- Save all artifacts to incident bucket and attach to INC card.
- Assign an owner for long-term fixes (allocator config, tenant limits, telemetry gaps).
- Draft a short blameless summary within 48 hours with timeline and artifacts.
- If tenant behavior was root cause: notify solutions engineering + customer success with recommended config changes and limits.

Follow-up mitigations and backlog candidates (examples):
- Per-tenant GPU soft-limits that reduce batch size automatically when memory/SM utilization crosses threshold.
- Eviction scoring improvement: include kernel-duration and memory-bandwidth metrics as first-class signals.
- Autoscaler: introduce smoothed metrics and add a circuit-breaker when multiple tenants are scaling simultaneously.
- Better out-of-band capture tooling: small agent that can collect 30s of dcgm/nvidia-smi/logs atomically and upload to incident store.

Human factors / communication guidance:
- Keep customer-facing teams informed during containment: single sentence status updates every 15 minutes until triage stabilizes.
- If an eviction affects SLAs, prepare compensation playbook but don’t promise until root cause validated.

Open questions and TODOs (for later refinement):
- Define exact thresholds for "disproportionate tenant" (50% is a draft number).
- Validate which allocator admin APIs are safe to expose to oncall; limit blast radius.
- Add example scripts to ops repo that automate snapshotting and labeling.

Recent example (context):
- Incident INC-2025-338 (Feb 12 2025): eu-west pool experienced 18% throughput loss for 22 minutes. Snapshot showed one legacy batcher process with repeated 30s kernels. Containment: throttled tenant and evicted two pods; throughput recovered in 6 minutes. Follow-ups: add per-tenant soft-limits and add kernel-duration into eviction score (SRE-5822).

Appendix: suggested places to copy artifacts to during an incident:
- S3: s3://redwood-incidents/inc-<id>/artifacts/
- Internal: gs://redwood-sre-temp/<pool>/<ts>/
- Slack thread: pin the summary + link to artifacts

If you pick this up on-call: add your short signature and timestamp at top of a copy of this doc and paste the first containment decision into the incident card.

-- Aisha P. (draft, v0.3)
